source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured primary references. Current Kubernetes documentation supports startup/liveness/readiness purposes and actions, startup suppression, probe mechanisms/timing/thresholds, probe-level grace, pod/container states and conditions, readiness-gate conjunction/absence behavior, EndpointSlice ready/serving/terminating mapping, PostStart/PreStop/StopSignal timing and at-least-once hook delivery, native sidecar lifecycle/order, termination flow, disruption conditions, PDB scope/selector/availability semantics, drain, and preemption/PDB limitations. The chapter does not treat a passing probe, Ready Pod, ReadyToStartContainers condition, PDB, zero exit, hook completion, or endpoint status as proof of business correctness, traffic cessation, safe work completion, or abrupt-failure safety.

evidence: Checked L=(S,V,R,D,A,H,T,E,P,O,X), detection and termination bounds, readiness/gate and traffic-eligibility conjunctions, accepted-work cardinality, force-kill interval, and restart-amplification notation.

Checked tuple, indexed predicates, big conjunction, set cardinality, inequality, approximate upper bound, time-indexed state, and much-greater-than syntax with repository-compatible GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Startup, local liveness, container/pod readiness, endpoint eligibility, drain safety, and user outcome remain distinct.

evidence: Executed health-lifecycle-inventory and reproduced eight workloads, two startup probes, three liveness probes, six readiness probes, two external gates, and 360 total configured grace seconds.
Recomputed Exercise 3's conservative non-overlapped budget as 12+2+25+8+3+10=60 seconds and verified that any overlap requires implementation evidence.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The inventory is synthetic and explicitly disclaims predicate, timing, external registration, drain, work-preservation, and recovery evidence.

evidence: Expanded the eleven-element lifecycle model through startup, liveness, readiness, dependency capability, accepted work, hooks/signals, drain, endpoints, disruption, observation, and exceptions.
Expanded Pod Ready from container readiness and every gate, then expanded Service eligibility through selection, endpoint, programming, and reachability.
Expanded grace as propagation, hook, drain, flush, exit, and uncertainty, with concurrency accepted only when demonstrated.
Expanded safe exit from zero accepted unfinished work or durable unambiguous handoff, separately from exit code.
Checked restart amplification and verified a shared dependency failure can trigger more restarts than locally failed replicas.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The expressions model lifecycle obligations and do not guarantee kubelet timing, network propagation, or zero work loss.

evidence: Reviewed absent/slow/stuck startup, false live health thread, shared dependency outage, overload, probe timeout/flap, threshold one, expensive/side-effecting HTTP or exec checks, TCP false positives, blocked kubelet path, and sensitive probe output.

Reviewed absent/stale readiness gates, conflicting status writers, controller death, readiness fan-out, degraded capability, non-Service workers, rollout/PDB effects, and condition/control-plane versus business-outcome gaps.

Reviewed repeated/skipped/failed/hung PostStart/PreStop, PID-1 signal loss, nonstandard stop signals, grace exhaustion, stale endpoints/proxies/connections, long streams, queue leases, state flush, SIGKILL, OOM, node partition, and force deletion without fencing.

Reviewed ordinary versus native sidecar ordering, PDB selector/rounding/empty-selector/unhealthy-policy, direct deletion, rollout, preemption, taint/node-pressure eviction, node loss, maintenance block, restart backoff, and erased previous evidence.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Probe, dependency, traffic, hook, signal, abrupt-failure, multi-container, and disruption boundaries are explicit.

evidence: Traced separate predicates/actions through startup suppression, liveness restart, readiness withdrawal, capability degradation, business monitoring, drain, and termination.
Checked local-recovery and probe-safety invariants across dependency failure, overload, false positives, bounded cost, no side effects, and non-sensitive output.
Checked gate ownership/freshness and propagation through Pod conditions, EndpointSlices, proxies/load balancers, stale clients, and application new-work rejection.
Checked drain and abrupt-failure invariants across hooks/signals, accepted work, checkpoint/handoff, state protocols, sidecar order, grace/SIGKILL, node loss, and fencing.
Checked disruption/evidence invariants across PDB, replicas/topology/capacity, rollout/eviction/preemption, conditions, task outcomes, and temporal tests.
invariant_checking.notes: All declared predicate-separation, local-recovery, probe-safety, gate, drain, propagation, abrupt-failure, disruption, and evidence invariants remain consistent across examples and answers.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; lifecycle mechanisms are framed as an assurance structure with kubelet, runtime, propagation, application, client, storage, and operational assumptions.

evidence: The lifecycle inventory is labeled synthetic and disclaims operational equivalence.
Normative project documentation, practitioner synthesis, timing models, and scenario examples remain distinguishable.
Startup tails, detection, propagation, drain, accepted-work completion, restart amplification, disruption, and availability are presented as properties to measure, not observed results.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external lifecycle conformance test, load-balancer study, failure injection, drain measurement, security assessment, or production rollout is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently separates startup, locally recoverable liveness, traffic readiness, dependency capability, custom gates, endpoint propagation, work drain, graceful/abrupt termination, pod disruption, and user outcome.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can design and tune predicates/probes, interpret pod/container status, own readiness gates, implement PID-1 signals and idempotent hooks, budget/drain protocols, coordinate sidecars/PDBs, observe lifecycle, diagnose incidents, and test temporal safety.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from predicate design and state boundaries through probe types/mechanisms/tuning, gates, safe output, process/hooks, termination budgets, protocol drain, sidecars, restart/replacement/failover, PDB/disruptions, observation, diagnosis, testing, and platform contracts. Ten examples remain distinct; five exercises progress from workload design through audit, exact timing, rollout diagnosis, and robot-fleet transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
